title: Builder Pattern
subtitle: Separates the construction of a complex object from its representation, allowing the same construction process to create various representations.
keyTakeaways: Eliminates the 'Telescoping Constructor' anti-pattern where classes require constructors with 10+ overloaded parameters.
Enforces object immutability by collecting configuration parameters step-by-step and validating invariants prior to final instantiation in build().
Separates optional attributes from mandatory constraints while providing clean, readable fluent method chaining.

sections.heading: Preventing Telescoping Constructors and Mutation Bugs
sections.body: As domain entities accumulate dozens of optional settings, constructors become unmaintainable (e.g. `new HttpRequest(url, headers, timeout, retry, proxy, cookieJar, null, null, false)`). Passing multiple boolean and null arguments introduces severe caller bugs. The Builder pattern isolates configuration assembly, enforces required parameters, and produces an immutable target instance.
bullets: Fluent API: Self-documenting, chained method invocations improve code readability across engineering teams.
Fail-Fast Invariant Checking: All business constraint validations run atomically inside the build() method prior to object creation.
Thread Safety: The constructed entity can have only private final fields and no setters, making it inherently thread-safe.

tradeOffs.pros: Provides fluent readable code, supports partial construction, enables immutable target objects.
tradeOffs.cons: Requires duplicating all domain fields in the builder class; higher boilerplate overhead.
tradeOffs.bestFor: Complex domain entities, HTTP/gRPC client configurations, SQL/query generators.

tradeOffs.pros: Compact syntax (records), simple bean reflection support (frameworks like Jackson/Spring).
tradeOffs.cons: Setters expose mutable state causing concurrent race conditions; records with 10+ fields are hard to read at call sites.
tradeOffs.bestFor: Small DTOs with 2-4 fields, simple data mapping payloads.

interviewTip: In interviews, emphasize how Builder enables Immutability. Explain that in multi-threaded environments, an immutable object constructed via a Builder eliminates the need for synchronization locks.
